Review complete. Custody verified before and after: manifest SHA-256 matches, all 1378 files byte-identical, no repository or snapshot writes (all output under `/tmp`).

## Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED

**Everything the v3 design review and the v1 application review asked for in the design layer is corrected.** I independently verified, not assumed: MUST-A, SHOULD-A, ADV-i..vi, N-1..5, A-1..5, CX-01..07, the original MUST-1..3/SHOULD-1..10, and application-review S-1/S-2. All four suites plus integration reproduce exactly (397 / 444+9 / 101 / 1206 / 311), all ten reports byte-identical, every claimed count matched.

The three new acts I was asked to review substantively are real and complete: admission §5's seven boundary dispositions carry no deferral phrase and cover the four items the application review found uncovered; security S16 maps **one-to-one** onto architecture file 05 (5 preserve / 5 distinctions / 6 prohibitions — checked item-for-item, not by term counting), including the no-write-preinitialization vs. explicit-default-first-write join and foreign-state refusal before any write.

**One MUST blocks acceptance — MUST-A(v4), in D-372's own SARIF/G17 re-entry.** The act names four commands; the inventory gives `repair-verify` no `verdict`, `deficiency` or `findings` parity field although it is non-advisory and seals an authoritative Run. Driving the real renderer:

```
repair-verify  runProperties = {'verdict': None, 'deficiency': None}   results = 1
audit          runProperties = {'verdict': 'x-verdict', 'deficiency': None}
```

Root cause is one expression with two sourcing rules: `results` reads the **unfiltered** envelope, `runProperties` reads the **parity-filtered** projection. And `default`, `audit` and `repair-verify` have **no SARIF render case at all** — only `analyze` does — so no unit or integration check can expose it.

★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────
- This is the "self-consistent but wrong" shape: every piece passes its own checks (rows well-formed, parity holds, advisory commands correctly excluded) because `parity_holds` compares only *declared* fields and therefore cannot see a renderer emitting data outside that set.
- It was findable only by executing the join, not by reading either side: the inventory looks complete, the renderer law looks complete, and the contradiction lives in their composition.
- Count-based evidence actively hid it — 1206 workflow checks pass while the newly re-entered surface is exercised for one of four commands.
─────────────────────────────────────────────────

**Scoped review-owner dispositions** (new full-product scope; historical 2026-08-13 grades untouched, none inherited): DR-201 ACCEPT · **DR-202 CHANGES_REQUIRED** (owns MUST-A(v4)) · DR-203 ACCEPT · DR-204 ACCEPT · DR-205 ACCEPT. AR-13 and AR-16 CHANGES_REQUIRED, other fourteen ACCEPT; FW-13 CHANGES_REQUIRED, other fourteen ACCEPT; DR-011-R08/R13 CHANGES_REQUIRED, R10 correctly left open for consumer B. DR-003 timing disposition affirmed as proposed; condition 5 remains NOT MET.

Five advisories: duplicate integration check id (311 checks, 310 ids); the new 1025-root evidence uses only the standalone instrument (I confirmed the operational path works myself); a legible-but-confusing `A / B / B` cell in native §10; FW-11 owned by inherited file 13 §6; and `discovery()` having no closed-input admission.

**Honesty note:** 36 of my 114 probes failed on *my* selectors, not the subject (wrong schema file, a `config` key the discovery input lacks, a truncated regex). Each is superseded by a named corrected probe that passes; I retained the failures rather than deleting them, and no finding rests on one.

I did not perform blind consumer B and claim no application acceptance.
